image:image.image:caption: Beautifully decorated with fresh organic strawberries Raw Hazelnut Cardamom and Strawberry Layered Cake, so gorgeous so tasty

image:image.image:title: Beautifully decorated with fresh organic strawberries Raw Hazelnut Cardamom and Strawberry Layered Cake, so gorgeous so tasty
image:image.image:caption: Beautifully decorated with fresh organic strawberries Raw Hazelnut Cardamom and Strawberry Layered Cake, so gorgeous so tasty

image:image.image:title: After pressing the bottom layer of the cake batter in, pour the strawberry puree over the cake. Tap the pan on the counter lightly to work out any air bubbles and so it will rest evenly. Place in the freezer till firm.
image:image.image:caption: After pressing the bottom layer of the cake batter in, pour the strawberry puree over the cake. Tap the pan on the counter lightly to work out any air bubbles and so it will rest evenly. Place in the freezer till firm.

image:image.image:title: Once the strawberry layer is hard, place the top layer of the cake on top. Gently press evenly and firmly. Return to the freezer for 4+ hours, or until frozen. This will help with frosting.
image:image.image:caption: Once the strawberry layer is hard, place the top layer of the cake on top. Gently press evenly and firmly. Return to the freezer for 4+ hours, or until frozen. This will help with frosting.

image:image.image:title: Now we are ready to put the first, thin layer of frosting on the cake. This is what we call the "crumb" layer. It looks a bit rough at first, but the second layer of frosting will more smooth. Place the cake back in the freezer for about 15 minutes.
image:image.image:caption: Now we are ready to put the first, thin layer of frosting on the cake. This is what we call the "crumb" layer. It looks a bit rough at first, but the second layer of frosting will more smooth. Place the cake back in the freezer for about 15 minutes.

image:image.image:caption: Hidden inside those fat, long pods are handfuls of delicious beans, but they make you work for it. All good things in life require a little work, and work builds character, right? So think of these as a character building bean! I am not selling this very well, am I? But seriously, despite the seemingly never-ending shucking involved, fava beans have a buttery goodness that you don’t find in other beans, making the toilsome undertaking a true treasure hunt.

image:image.image:title: creating zucchini noodle letters for the raw vegan Vegetable Alphabet Soup
image:image.image:caption: creating zucchini noodle letters for the raw vegan Vegetable Alphabet Soup

image:image.image:title: To make the zucchini alphabet "noodles", you will need a mandolin, zucchini, and alphabet fondant cutters. If you don't own a mandolin, you can use a sharp paring knife and cut thin strips. Be slow and careful. If you can't find organic zucchini be sure to peel the zucchini. Slice the zucchini lengthwise about 1/8" thick. If your zucchini has large seeds, only slice down to those. If you have large seeds it will be mushy when trying to cut out the letters. Don't worry though, that seeded part will get used in the rest of the recipe, so nothing goes to waste.
image:image.image:caption: To make the zucchini alphabet "noodles", you will need a mandolin, zucchini, and alphabet fondant cutters. If you don't own a mandolin, you can use a sharp paring knife and cut thin strips. Be slow and careful. If you can't find organic zucchini be sure to peel the zucchini. Slice the zucchini lengthwise about 1/8" thick. If your zucchini has large seeds, only slice down to those. If you have large seeds it will be mushy when trying to cut out the letters. Don't worry though, that seeded part will get used in the rest of the recipe, so nothing goes to waste.
